title: Subscription Price Increases: How to Notice Them and What to Do
seoTitle: Subscription Price Increases: How to Notice and Respond
description: Subscription prices go up regularly, often with a short email you might miss. How to spot price increases and decide whether to keep, switch or cancel.
lede: Price increases rarely arrive with a fanfare. A short email, a notice in the app, and next month you pay more. Here is how to stay on top of them.
content:
Streaming, music, cloud and software services raise their prices from time to time. Each increase is usually small: a dollar or two a month. But spread across several subscriptions, small increases change your yearly total noticeably.

How companies announce price changes

  • Email, often with a subject line that does not mention the price.
  • In-app notices that appear when you open the app.
  • Google Play or Apple notifications for subscriptions billed through the app stores. For some increases, the store asks you to accept the new price before it applies.
  • Your statement, which is the moment many people first notice.

Most services announce changes some time before they take effect, which gives you a window to decide.

How to spot increases early

  1. Search your email every few months for "price", "pricing" and "changes to your plan".
  2. Read app store notices carefully rather than tapping "OK".
  3. Compare your statement with the price you expect. A subscription tracker makes this easy, because you know what each charge should be.

What to do when a price goes up

You have more options than keeping or cancelling:

  • Switch to a cheaper tier, such as an ad-supported plan or a plan with fewer screens.
  • Switch to yearly billing if you use the service every day. The yearly plan may still be cheaper per month.
  • Share a family plan if the service offers one.
  • Rotate with other services instead of paying all year.
  • Cancel, if the new price is more than the service is worth to you.

Keeping your tracker accurate

When a price changes, update it in RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android. Your monthly and yearly totals update straight away, and future reminders show the new amount, so the number in the notification matches the charge.

A tip: when you get a price change email, add the new price and its start date to the subscription’s notes. When the renewal reminder arrives, you have the context right there.

A yearly check

Once a year, look through every subscription and ask:

  • What do I pay now, and what did I pay a year ago?
  • Is there a cheaper plan that still fits how I use it?
  • Would I sign up again today at this price?

Price increases are normal. Paying them without noticing is optional.

title: Plan Your Holiday Streaming Without Paying for Every Service
seoTitle: Holiday Streaming on a Budget: Plan Your Subscriptions
description: Christmas films, new seasons and sports all land on different services. How to plan holiday streaming, use trials wisely and avoid a January full of charges.
lede: The holidays are peak streaming season. With a little planning, you can watch what you want without collecting subscriptions you pay for until spring.
content:
December is when streaming services release holiday films, finish big seasons and run their most generous trials. It is also when many people sign up for two or three services they forget about until the January statement.

A short plan avoids that.

Step 1: Make a watch list

Before signing up for anything, write down what you actually want to watch over the holidays: the Christmas classics, the new season, the big match. Next to each, note which service has it. Many titles are on services you already pay for.

Step 2: Choose one or two services for December

Group your list by service. Usually one or two services cover most of it. Subscribe to those for December and leave the rest for another month.

Step 3: Use trials on purpose

Holiday trials are a good way to watch a specific series or film for free. Use them for what is on your list, not for browsing.

  • Cancel right after signing up if the service allows it. On Google Play, you usually keep access until the end of the trial.
  • Note the end date and the price after the trial straight away.
  • Avoid trials that convert to yearly plans unless you are sure.

Step 4: Track every holiday subscription

Holiday sign-ups are the ones most often forgotten, because they happen during a busy, distracted time and end in January.

Add each trial and new subscription to RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, the day you start it. Trials appear at the top of Home with a countdown and the price after the trial. Set reminders three days and one day before each one ends.

Step 5: Decide in early January

When the reminders arrive, choose for each service:

  • Keep it if you will keep watching.
  • Cancel it if the holiday binge is over, then mark it as cancelled in RenewRadar.
  • Rotate, keeping one service for January and switching later. See our guide to subscription rotation.

Do not forget sports passes and add-ons

Holiday sports passes, premium channels and add-ons often renew monthly at a higher price. Track them like any other subscription, with an early reminder.

Enjoy the holidays

The goal is not to watch less. It is to make sure December’s entertainment does not quietly become February’s bill.

title: Gift Subscriptions: What Happens When They End
seoTitle: Gift Subscriptions: What Happens When They End?
description: Gift subscriptions are popular presents, but some turn into paid plans when they run out. How to give and receive them without surprise charges.
lede: A year of music, a few months of streaming, a meal kit for three months: gift subscriptions make great presents. Here is what to check so they do not become a surprise bill.
content:
Gift subscriptions are an easy present: a gift card for a streaming service, a year of a music app, a few months of a box delivery. But they work in different ways, and the end of the gift is not always the end of the payments.

Two kinds of gift subscriptions

Prepaid gifts

The giver pays once for a fixed period, often with a gift card or code. When the receiver redeems it, some services ask for a payment method. If the receiver adds one, the subscription can continue automatically at the regular price when the gift period ends.

Gifted plans

The giver adds someone to their own plan or pays for a subscription in the receiver’s name. In this case, the giver keeps paying until they cancel, sometimes long after the receiver stopped using it.

If you received a gift subscription

The gift period is essentially a free trial with a longer end date. Treat it like one:

  1. Check your account to see whether a payment method is on file.
  2. Find the exact end date of the gift period.
  3. Track it. In RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, add it with Free trial switched on, the gift end date as the trial end, and the regular price as the price after the trial. It appears in the Trials section with a countdown.
  4. Set reminders a week and a day before the gift ends.

When the reminder arrives, decide whether you want to keep paying yourself.

If you gave a gift subscription

If you bought a one-time prepaid gift, there is usually nothing to track. If you pay for someone on your own plan, or bought a subscription that renews, add it to your tracker:

  • Set Used for to Personal and write who it is for in the notes, such as "Gift for Mum".
  • Choose a reminder before each renewal, so you can check whether it is still used and wanted.

Gift cards for app stores

A Google Play gift card adds credit to the receiver’s account. Subscriptions paid from that balance continue as long as there is credit, and some then switch to the next payment method on file. If you use a Play balance for subscriptions, keep an eye on the renewal dates as the balance runs down.

Give the gift of fewer surprises

When giving a subscription, a short note helps: "This runs until March. Cancel before then if you do not want to keep it." It is a small kindness that saves the receiver a surprise charge.

title: Holiday Free Trials End in January. Here Is How to Be Ready
seoTitle: Holiday Free Trials End in January: Avoid Surprise Charges
description: Trials started in December all end in January, right when the bills arrive. How to keep track of holiday trials and decide before the first charges.
lede: Trials started over the holidays end in January, the month when everyone checks their bank balance. A little preparation now saves a lot of stress then.
content:
December is the busiest month for free trials. New phones and tablets come with offers, streaming services run holiday promotions, and fitness apps get downloaded for new year resolutions. All of those trials end in January.

Why January is the danger month

  • Several trials end close together. It is easy to lose track of which ends when.
  • Holiday spending is already high. Unexpected charges are the last thing you need.
  • You are back at work and busy. The trials you started on a relaxed afternoon end on a hectic weekday.
  • New devices bring bundled trials that you may not even remember accepting.

Get ready in ten minutes

1. List every trial you started

Check Google Play’s Subscriptions page, your email for "trial" and "welcome", and the setup screens of any new devices. Bundled trials for music, cloud storage and streaming are common with new phones.

2. Record the end date and price after each trial

Look for whether each trial becomes monthly or yearly. A yearly conversion can be a big January charge.

3. Put them all in one place

In RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, add each one with Free trial switched on. The Trials section at the top of Home lists them by end date, with days left and the price that starts afterwards.

4. Set two reminders per trial

Three days and one day before the end gives you time to decide and a last chance to act. Reminders arrive on your phone even without the app open.

5. Cancel the clear no’s now

If you already know you do not want to keep a trial, cancel it today. Most services, including subscriptions through Google Play, let you keep access until the trial ends.

When the reminders arrive

For each trial, ask: did I use it in the last week? Would I pay the full price for it? If not, cancel and mark it as cancelled in RenewRadar. If yes, keep it, and RenewRadar tracks it as a regular subscription from then on.

A calmer January

Holiday trials are a nice way to try new things at a relaxed time of year. With every end date in one list and a reminder before each one, January’s statement only contains what you chose.

title: Shared and Family Subscriptions: Who Pays for What?
seoTitle: How to Track Shared and Family Subscriptions
description: Family plans save money, but they make it harder to know who pays for what. How to track shared subscriptions and avoid paying twice.
lede: Family and shared plans are one of the best ways to save on subscriptions. They are also one of the easiest ways to end up paying twice.
content:
Family and duo plans let several people share one subscription for much less than separate plans. Music, video, cloud storage, games and even some software offer them. They are a great deal, as long as everyone knows how they work.

The common mix-ups

  • Paying twice. Someone joins the family plan but forgets to cancel their own individual plan.
  • Paying for someone who left. A family member moved out or stopped using it, but is still on the plan.
  • Unclear billing. Nobody is sure whose card the plan is on.
  • Trials on the wrong card. A child or partner starts a trial using a shared payment method.

Decide who tracks what

The simplest rule: the person who pays tracks the subscription. Everyone else does not need to, unless they reimburse the payer.

If you pay for a family plan, add it to your subscription tracker with the full price. If someone pays you back each month, note it.

Tracking shared plans in RenewRadar

RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, does not need accounts or sharing to handle family plans. Each person keeps their own list on their own phone, and the payer tracks the shared plan.

A few tips:

  • Use the notes field for who is on the plan and who pays what, such as "Family plan: me, Ana, Leo. Ana pays $5."
  • Set a reminder before the renewal to check that everyone still uses it.
  • When someone joins your plan, remind them to cancel their own individual subscription, and to mark it as cancelled in their RenewRadar.

Google Play family payment methods

Google Play lets families share a payment method through a family group. Purchases and subscriptions by family members can be charged to that shared method, sometimes with approval settings for children. If you manage a family group, review its subscriptions in Google Play from time to time and track the ones you pay for.

Splitting costs fairly

If you split a plan, the yearly total helps conversations stay simple: "This costs $203.88 a year, so $67.96 each." RenewRadar shows each subscription’s monthly and yearly cost, which makes splitting easy to calculate.

Review once a year

Family situations change. Once a year, check each shared plan: who is on it, who uses it, and whether a cheaper plan now fits better.

title: Keep Work and Business Subscriptions Separate From Personal Ones
seoTitle: Track Work and Business Subscriptions Separately
description: Freelancers and small business owners often pay for tools from one card. How to label work, business and personal subscriptions and keep them apart.
lede: When your design tool, your music plan and your hosting all bill the same card, it gets hard to know what is a business expense. Labels fix that.
content:
Freelancers, contractors and small business owners often pay for work tools and personal services from the same card or the same Google account. Over time, it becomes hard to answer simple questions: what does my business spend on software each month? Which of these charges can I claim?

Why keep them apart

  • Clear business costs. You know what your work tools cost per month and per year.
  • Easier taxes and bookkeeping. Business subscriptions are often deductible expenses in many countries. Check with an accountant for your situation.
  • Better decisions. Personal subscriptions are judged by enjoyment; work ones by whether they earn their cost.
  • Easier handover. If a business tool is billed to you personally, a list makes it easier to move it to a company card.

The three labels

RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, has a Used for field with three options: Personal, Work and Business. It defaults to Personal.

On the Home screen, Work and Business subscriptions show a small briefcase or building badge on the service circle, so you can tell them apart at a glance.

What counts as work or business?

  • Work: tools you pay for yourself to do your job, such as a design app, a writing tool or a course platform you use for work.
  • Business: subscriptions for your own company or freelance business, such as hosting, domains, accounting software and team tools.
  • Personal: everything else.

Use whichever split makes sense for you and your accountant.

Add the details you will need later

The notes field is useful for:

  • Which card or account the subscription is billed to.
  • The invoice email address or where to download receipts.
  • Who in your team uses it.

Exporting for your records

RenewRadar Pro can export your full list as a CSV file, including each subscription’s label, price, currency, cycle and next date. Open it in a spreadsheet, filter by Work or Business, and you have a list of recurring business costs for your bookkeeping.

A tip for multi-currency tools

Many software tools bill in US dollars. Enter each subscription in the currency it is billed in. RenewRadar keeps a separate total for each currency, so your numbers match your statements. See our guide to multi-currency subscriptions.

The payoff

A few seconds of labelling when you add a subscription saves hours at tax time and makes it obvious which tools are worth keeping.

title: Forgotten Subscriptions: 9 Places They Hide
seoTitle: How to Find Forgotten Subscriptions: 9 Places to Check
description: Forgotten subscriptions hide in app stores, PayPal, phone bills and old email accounts. Nine places to check to find every recurring charge.
lede: The subscriptions you remember are not the problem. The ones you forgot are. Here is where to look for them.
content:
Most people can list their main subscriptions from memory. The ones that cost money for months without anyone noticing are those billed in unusual places. Here are nine places to look.

1. Google Play

Play Store, profile picture, Payments & subscriptions, Subscriptions. Check every Google account you use, not just the main one.

2. Apple

If you have ever had an iPhone or iPad, check Settings, your name, Subscriptions, or your Apple account on the web. Subscriptions keep running even after you switch to Android.

3. PayPal and other wallets

PayPal keeps a list of automatic payments in its settings. Many services you signed up for with "Pay with PayPal" are there.

4. Card and bank statements

Go through the last three months and look for amounts that repeat. Yearly charges will not show up in three months, so also search the last year for well-known service names.

5. Your phone carrier bill

Carriers can bill games, streaming bundles and premium services directly to your phone bill. These are easy to miss because they are combined with your plan.

6. Old email accounts

Search old inboxes for "receipt", "renewal", "subscription", "trial" and "your plan". Services keep billing even if you no longer read that email address.

7. Memberships with perks

Shopping memberships, delivery passes and warehouse clubs often renew yearly and include streaming or music perks. Make sure you are not also paying for those perks separately.

8. Software, domains and hosting

Antivirus, VPNs, password managers, website domains and hosting usually renew yearly, often at a higher price than the first year.

9. Other people’s devices

Children’s games, a partner’s app or a parent’s tablet may have subscriptions billed to your card or your family payment method.

What to do once you find them

Put everything in one list. RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, is built for this: add each subscription with its price, cycle and next date, and write where it is billed in the notes, such as "PayPal" or "carrier bill". That tells you exactly where to cancel later.

Cancel what you do not need, then mark it as cancelled in the app. Cancelled items move to their own list and do not count toward the free limit, so you keep a record of what you stopped.

Stop new ones from hiding

From now on, add every new subscription and free trial on the day you start it. RenewRadar reminds you before each charge, so nothing gets the chance to hide again.

title: Weekly Subscriptions Cost More Than You Think
seoTitle: Weekly App Subscriptions: The Real Monthly Cost
description: A weekly price looks small, but a weekly plan is usually the most expensive way to pay. How to calculate the real cost and when to switch plans.
lede: Many apps advertise a low weekly price. It sounds like loose change, but over a month, and especially over a year, weekly plans add up fast.
content:
Weekly subscriptions are common in mobile apps: photo editors, VPNs, language learning, fitness and AI tools. The price is shown per week to make it look small. But there are 52 weeks in a year, and about 4.33 in a month.

Doing the arithmetic

To compare a weekly plan with monthly or yearly options:

  • Monthly cost: weekly price x 52 / 12.
  • Yearly cost: weekly price x 52.

A $2.99 weekly plan is about $12.96 a month and $155.48 a year. If the same app offers a yearly plan for $39.99, the weekly plan costs almost four times as much over a year.

Why apps use weekly plans

  • A small number on the purchase screen feels easy to accept.
  • Short trials lead into them. A three-day trial followed by a weekly plan is a common pattern.
  • People forget them. Weekly charges are frequent but small, so each one barely registers.

When a weekly plan makes sense

  • You need the app for a short project, a trip or a single week.
  • You will cancel straight after.

For anything you will use longer than a month or two, a monthly or yearly plan is almost always cheaper.

How to spot weekly plans you already have

Check Google Play’s Subscriptions page. The price shows the billing period, such as "$2.99/week". Also look at your statements for small charges that repeat every seven days.

Tracking weekly plans in RenewRadar

In RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, choose Weekly as the billing cycle. The app converts it to a monthly figure in your totals using the same formula, weekly x 52 / 12, so a weekly plan appears at its true monthly cost next to everything else.

A reminder one day before each weekly charge is usually enough. If you only need the app for a short time, set a reminder and cancel as soon as you are done.

The takeaway

Always convert a weekly price into a monthly or yearly cost before you accept it. If you will use the app for more than a few weeks, choose the longer plan, or look for an alternative without a weekly price.

seoTitle: Pause vs Cancel a Subscription: Which Should You Choose?
description: Many services let you pause instead of cancel. What pausing really does, when it is better than cancelling, and how to track both in RenewRadar.
lede: Some services offer a pause button when you try to leave. Sometimes it is the right choice. Often, it just delays the decision.
content:
When you go to cancel a subscription, many services offer an alternative: pause it for one, two or three months. Gyms, meal kits, streaming services and Google Play subscriptions all use pauses. It sounds harmless, but it works differently from cancelling.

What pausing usually means

  • No charges during the pause.
  • Your account, preferences and history are kept.
  • Billing restarts automatically at the end of the pause, usually without another confirmation.

That last point is the catch. A pause is like a free trial in reverse: doing nothing at the end means paying again.

When to pause

  • You know you will be back soon, for example after a trip or a busy month.
  • The service has a discount or old price you would lose by cancelling.
  • Your data or progress would be lost if you cancelled.

When to cancel

  • You are not sure you will come back.
  • You are rotating services and will return only when something new appears.
  • The pause would end at an inconvenient time, such as just before a holiday.

Remember that cancelling usually keeps your access until the end of the period you paid for, and many services keep your account so you can return later.

Tracking a pause

A pause needs a reminder before it ends, just like a trial. Otherwise, billing restarts quietly.

RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, has a Pause button on each subscription’s detail screen. A paused subscription stays on Home, dimmed, with no upcoming reminders and no effect on your totals. When the service starts billing again, tap Resume and set the next renewal date.

Because a paused item in RenewRadar has no reminders, add a note with the date the service’s pause ends. Or keep it active with the restart date as the next renewal, so you get a reminder before billing resumes.

Tracking a cancellation

When you cancel, tap Mark as cancelled. The subscription moves to the Cancelled list at the bottom of Home. It stops counting in your totals and toward the free limit of five. If you come back later, open it and tap Restore.

The simple rule

Pause when you know when you are coming back. Cancel when you do not. Either way, make sure something reminds you before the charges start again.

title: Your Subscription Year in Review: A 15-Minute End-of-Year Check
seoTitle: End-of-Year Subscription Review in 15 Minutes
description: A quick end-of-year review of everything you pay for: what you used, what you forgot, what is renewing in January and what to change for next year.
lede: Between the holidays is a quiet time to look back at the year's subscriptions. Fifteen minutes now can set up a cheaper, calmer next year.
content:
The end of the year is a natural time to review what you spend. Subscriptions are a good place to start, because small monthly decisions add up to big yearly numbers.

You do not need a spreadsheet or an afternoon. Here is a review that takes about fifteen minutes.

1. Look at your yearly total

Add up what you pay per year across all subscriptions. If you use RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, the yearly total is at the top of the Home screen.

Ask yourself: is this number what you expected? Higher? Lower?

2. Check spending by category

Which category costs the most: streaming, software, music, fitness, games? The Stats screen in RenewRadar breaks your spending down by category.

Category totals often reveal patterns, like several services that do the same thing.

3. Mark what you actually used

Go through the list and note, honestly, which subscriptions you used in the last month. Be strict. "I might use it" does not count.

4. List what renews in January

January is a heavy month for renewals: holiday trials end, yearly plans started last January renew, and new year offers begin. Sort your list by next renewal and look at the next four weeks.

RenewRadar Pro includes a report of the charges expected over the next 12 months, which shows at a glance which months will be expensive.

5. Pick one change for next year

Do not try to fix everything. Choose one change, such as:

  • Cancel the subscription you used least this year.
  • Switch your most-used service from monthly to yearly.
  • Rotate two streaming services instead of keeping both.
  • Turn on reminders for every yearly plan.

Celebrate the good ones

A review is not only about cutting. Notice the subscriptions that gave you real value this year: the music you listened to every day, the app that helped you work. Those are worth paying for.

Make next year’s review easier

If you track subscriptions as you go, next year’s review takes five minutes instead of fifteen. Add each new subscription and trial the day you start it, mark cancellations as you make them, and let reminders handle the dates in between.

title: Is RenewRadar Safe? How Your Data Stays on Your Phone

description: What data RenewRadar stores, where it is kept, what the app sends over the internet and what permissions it needs. A plain explanation of the app's privacy.

RenewRadar is a subscription tracker and reminder app for Android made by Pixel DevCode. Your subscription list says a lot about you, so we designed the app to know as little as possible about you. Here is exactly how it works.

What you enter, and where it is stored

Everything you add, such as names, prices, dates, categories and notes, is stored in the app’s private storage on your phone. Other apps cannot read it. There is no copy on our servers, because we do not run a server that receives your list.

No account, no bank connection

RenewRadar never asks for your name, email address, bank login or card details. There is no sign-up. Nothing is read from your bank or card accounts.

What goes over the internet

RenewRadar makes only two kinds of network requests:

  1. Service suggestions: about once a week, the app downloads an updated list of popular service names, categories and usual billing cycles from our website. It is a plain file download that contains nothing about you.
  2. Pro purchase status: Google Play and RevenueCat, our purchase provider, confirm whether you bought Pro. This uses an anonymous app user ID and the purchase status only.

Your subscriptions, prices, dates and notes are never part of these requests.

Permissions

RenewRadar asks for one permission: to show notifications, because that is how your reminders reach you. It also uses an internet connection for the two requests above.

RenewRadar does not ask for location, contacts, camera, microphone, photos or files.

When does your data leave the phone?

Only when you choose. Pro users can export a CSV file of their list. Android’s share sheet then asks where to send it: a drive, an email, a messaging app. RenewRadar does not upload it anywhere by itself.

What happens if you uninstall?

Uninstalling the app deletes its data from your phone. Because there is no cloud copy, the list is gone unless you exported it first. Pro can be restored on any phone with the same Google account.

Is it safe from other apps on the phone?

Android keeps each app’s private storage separate. As long as your phone is protected by a screen lock and kept up to date, other apps cannot read RenewRadar’s data.

Make sure you have the real app

Several apps and websites use similar names. The real RenewRadar is written as one word, published by Pixel DevCode, listed on Google Play as RenewRadar: Subscriptions with the app ID com.pixeldevcode.renewradar, and has its website at renewradar.pixeldevcode.com. If you add up your subscriptions and divide by twelve, you get a tidy monthly average. Real life is lumpier. A month with a yearly software renewal, a membership and an annual storage plan can cost several times more than a quiet month.

Why some months are expensive

  • Yearly plans all renew in the month you first bought them.
  • Holiday and new year sign-ups cluster renewals in December and January.
  • Quarterly plans add a bump every three months.
  • Intro offers ending raise prices from a specific month.

What the 12-month report shows

RenewRadar Pro includes detailed reports. One of them lists the charges you can expect in each of the next 12 months, based on every active subscription’s price, billing cycle and next renewal date. If you pay in more than one currency, each currency gets its own view.

It answers questions like:

  • Which month will be the most expensive?
  • Which yearly renewals are coming up, and when?
  • How much should I set aside before a big month?

How to use it

Spot the peaks early

A yearly renewal you notice three months ahead is a decision. One you notice on the day is a surprise.

Spread or move renewals

Some services let you switch billing dates or move from yearly to monthly. If three big renewals land in the same month, moving one can make budgeting easier.

Set money aside

If you know April will cost an extra $140, putting a little aside each month is easier than finding it all at once.

Decide before you are charged

When a big renewal is a month away, check whether you still use it, whether there is a cheaper plan, and whether a better deal exists. Then set a reminder 14 days before, so the final decision happens in time.

Combining it with reminders

Most people know their biggest single subscription. Fewer know their biggest subscription category. That second number is often more revealing.

Why categories help

  • They reveal overlap. Three cloud storage plans or two music services stand out immediately.
  • They show priorities. If streaming costs more than fitness and learning combined, is that what you want?
  • They make goals concrete. "Spend less on subscriptions" is vague. "Cut streaming from $45 to $25 a month" is a plan.

The categories in RenewRadar

The Stats screen shows your monthly and yearly spending, split by category. A few details:

  • Every cycle is normalised. Weekly, quarterly and yearly plans are converted to monthly figures, so categories compare fairly.

How to use your category totals

Look for duplicates

Check each category for services that do the same job. Two video services might both be worth it. Two cloud storage plans rarely are.

Set a category budget

Pick a monthly amount for your biggest category and use it to choose between services, for example by rotating streaming services instead of keeping them all.

Compare with value

A large software category may be fine if those tools earn you money. Mark them as Work or Business with the Used for label to keep them apart from personal spending.

Choosing categories for unusual subscriptions

Start with the totals

title: Managing Subscriptions on a Student Budget
seoTitle: Managing Subscriptions on a Student Budget
description: Students juggle streaming, music, study apps and free trials on a tight budget. Practical tips to pay less and avoid surprise charges.
lede: Student budgets are tight, and subscriptions are everywhere: music, streaming, study tools, cloud storage. A few habits keep them affordable.
content:
Students are a favourite audience for subscriptions: music, streaming, note-taking apps, language learning, cloud storage, design tools. Many offer discounts, but on a student budget even discounted plans add up, and a forgotten trial can hurt.

1. Use student discounts, and track when they end

Many music, streaming and software services offer student pricing. These discounts usually need re-verification every year and end when you graduate. When the discount ends, the subscription often continues at the full price.

Add the date your student status needs renewing, or when the discount ends, to your tracker so it does not catch you out.

2. Check what your school already gives you

Universities and colleges often provide office software, cloud storage, research tools and sometimes design or coding tools for free. Check before paying for your own.

3. Share plans

Family and duo plans can cut the cost per person a lot. Make sure everyone knows who pays and that people cancel their individual plans when they join.

4. Rotate entertainment

You do not need every streaming service at once. Pick one for the month, watch what you want, then switch.

5. Be careful with free trials

Free trials are tempting on a tight budget, but a forgotten trial is an unexpected charge. Track every trial the day you start it, with a reminder before it ends. If you only want the trial, cancel right after signing up when the service allows you to keep access until the end.

6. Avoid weekly app plans

Weekly plans in apps can cost several times more than monthly or yearly ones over time. Always check the monthly equivalent.

A free way to keep track

RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, is free for up to five subscriptions and trials, which covers many students completely. Cancelled items do not count toward that limit.

You get:

  • Reminders before each renewal and before each free trial ends.
  • A countdown for every trial, with the price after the trial.
  • Monthly and yearly totals, so you can see your subscriptions as part of your budget.

There is no account to create and no bank to connect, which also makes it a good fit if you are not ready to link a student bank account to an app.

The student rule of thumb

Before any new subscription, ask: would I pay for this at the full price after the discount or trial ends? If not, set a reminder, or skip it.

Freelancers often need a stack of tools: something to design, something to write, somewhere to host work, somewhere to store files, and something to send invoices. Each one is a subscription, and many are billed yearly in US dollars.

The goal is not the smallest tool stack. It is a stack where every subscription earns its place, and nothing renews without you deciding it should.

Note what your subscriptions cost per year at the start of January. Check again in June and December. Watching the number over time is one of the simplest ways to keep it reasonable.

title: Billed by Google Play, Apple or the Website? Why It Matters
seoTitle: App Store vs Website Subscriptions: Where You Are Billed
description: The same service can bill you through Google Play, Apple or its own website. Why it matters for prices, cancelling and refunds, and how to keep track.
lede: Where you subscribe decides where you cancel, how refunds work and sometimes what you pay. It is worth knowing for every subscription you have.
content:
Most popular services let you subscribe in more than one way: inside the Android app through Google Play, inside the iPhone app through Apple, or on their website with a card or PayPal. The service is the same, but the billing is not.

Why it matters

Cancelling

You cancel where you are billed. A subscription bought through Google Play cannot be cancelled on the service’s website, and a website subscription will not appear in Google Play. Uninstalling the app cancels nothing.

Refunds

Refund requests go to whoever billed you: Google, Apple or the service. Each has different rules.

Price

Prices can differ. App store prices are set in local currency and may include taxes. Website prices are sometimes lower because the service avoids app store fees, but may be in US dollars, with card fees for foreign currency.

Visibility

App store subscriptions are listed in one place: Google Play’s or Apple’s Subscriptions page. Website subscriptions are spread across many accounts and emails.

How to find out where you are billed

  • Your statement: "Google Play" or "Apple.com/bill" in the description means app store billing.
  • The confirmation email: the sender shows who billed you.
  • Google Play’s Subscriptions page: if it is listed there, Play bills you.

Keep a note of it

The simplest habit: write down where each subscription is billed when you add it to your tracker.

In RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, use the notes field, for example "Google Play", "Website, Visa ending 4421" or "PayPal". When a reminder arrives and you decide to cancel, you know exactly where to go.

Which should you choose?

  • App store billing is convenient: one place to see and cancel everything, and familiar refund processes.
  • Website billing can be cheaper and gives access to plans that app stores do not offer.

Either is fine, as long as you know which you chose. Our guide to cancelling a free trial covers the steps for each billing method.

title: Switched From iPhone to Android? Do Not Forget Your Subscriptions
seoTitle: Switched From iPhone to Android? Check Your Subscriptions
description: Apple subscriptions keep billing after you move to Android. How to find them, cancel or move them, and track everything on your new phone.
lede: A new Android phone does not cancel anything you subscribed to through Apple. Those subscriptions keep charging until you stop them.
content:
Moving from iPhone to Android is mostly about contacts, photos and apps. Subscriptions are easy to forget, and they are the part that keeps costing money.

Apple subscriptions do not move or stop

Subscriptions bought through the App Store are billed by Apple. They continue after you stop using your iPhone, even if you never open the app again. They do not appear in Google Play on your new phone.

The same is true in reverse: subscriptions billed through Google Play will not show up in Apple’s settings.

Find your Apple subscriptions

You can see them:

  • On your old iPhone or iPad: Settings, your name, Subscriptions.
  • On the web: sign in to your Apple account and look for Subscriptions.
  • In your email: search for receipts from Apple.

Decide what to do with each one

  • Keep using the service on Android? Many services work across platforms. You can keep the Apple subscription and sign in on Android, but managing it requires your Apple account. Many people prefer to cancel the Apple subscription and subscribe again through Google Play or the service’s website.
  • Do not need it any more? Cancel it in your Apple account.
  • iCloud storage? If you move your photos and files to another service, remember to cancel or downgrade the iCloud plan.

Cancel the old subscription before the new one starts, so you do not pay for both in the same month.

Easy things to miss

Start fresh with a tracker on Android

Switching phones is a good moment to put every subscription in one list, wherever it is billed. RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, keeps all of them together: Google Play, Apple, website, PayPal or carrier billing. Write where each one is billed in the notes, so you know where to cancel later.

You get reminders before each renewal, a countdown for every free trial, and monthly and yearly totals at the top of Home. There is no account to create and no bank to connect.

Already using RenewRadar and changing Android phones?

RenewRadar keeps your list on the phone, with no cloud sync. Before changing phones, Pro users can export a CSV copy. On the new phone, install RenewRadar and tap Restore purchase in Settings to unlock Pro again with the same Google account.

title: Why You Should Keep a Record of Cancelled Subscriptions
seoTitle: Keep a Record of Cancelled Subscriptions | RenewRadar
description: A list of what you cancelled helps you spot charges that should have stopped, rejoin services easily and see how much you have saved.
lede: When you cancel a subscription, the natural instinct is to forget it. Keeping a short record is more useful than it sounds.
content:
Cancelling a subscription feels like the end of the story. Often it is not. Charges can continue by mistake, you may want to return later, and it helps to remember what you stopped paying for.

Catch charges that should have stopped

Sometimes a cancellation does not go through: a confirmation was never completed, a family member re-subscribed, or the service made a mistake. If you have a record of what you cancelled and when, a charge that should not be there stands out immediately, and you have the date to quote when you ask for a refund.

Remember what you paid

Prices rise. If you return to a service a year later, knowing what you used to pay helps you judge the new price, or ask for a returning-customer offer.

Rejoin easily when you rotate

If you rotate streaming services, you will cancel and restart the same ones throughout the year. Keeping them in your tracker means you do not have to re-enter them every time.

See your progress

A list of cancelled subscriptions is a list of money you are no longer spending. It is satisfying, and it is a good reminder of why you keep track.

How RenewRadar handles cancelled subscriptions

In RenewRadar, the subscription tracker app for Android, open a subscription and tap Mark as cancelled after you cancel with the service.

  • The item leaves your active list and appears under Cancelled at the bottom of Home.
  • It stops counting in your monthly and yearly totals.
  • It does not count toward the free limit of five, so you can keep as many as you like for free.
  • Reminders for it are removed.

To bring one back, open it from the Cancelled list and tap Restore. RenewRadar sets it back to active and moves a past renewal date forward, so you only need to check the price and date.

A small habit

When you cancel, add a note with the date and how you cancelled, such as "Cancelled Jan 3 in Google Play". If something goes wrong later, you have everything you need in one place.

title: RenewRadar FAQ: Everything About the Subscription Tracker App
seoTitle: RenewRadar FAQ: The Subscription Tracker App Explained
description: Answers to common questions about RenewRadar, the subscription tracker and reminder app for Android by Pixel DevCode: features, pricing, privacy and more.
lede: Everything people ask about RenewRadar in one place: what it does, what it costs, how it protects your privacy and how to tell it apart from similarly named apps.
content:
What is RenewRadar?

RenewRadar is a subscription tracker and reminder app for Android, made by Pixel DevCode. You add your subscriptions and free trials, and it shows what they cost per month and per year and reminds you before each charge.

Is RenewRadar related to Renew Radar or Renewal Radar?

No. Several products use similar names. RenewRadar, written as one word, is the subscription tracker app by Pixel DevCode, and renewradar.pixeldevcode.com is its only website. It is not affiliated with renewradar.com, which is an SSL certificate monitoring service, or with other apps that have similar names.

Is RenewRadar free?

Yes, for up to five subscriptions and free trials, with reminders, trial countdowns and totals. Cancelled items do not count toward the limit. Pro removes the limit and adds detailed reports and CSV export.

How much is Pro?

A one-time payment of US$9.99, shown in your local currency on Google Play. It is not a subscription and never renews.

Does it connect to my bank?

No. RenewRadar never asks for bank logins or card details. You add each subscription yourself, which takes about a minute with suggestions for popular services.

Do I need an account?

No. There is no sign-up, email or password. Your list is stored only on your phone.

When do reminders arrive?

You choose for each subscription: 14, 7, 3 or 1 day before, or on the day, at 9 in the morning. You can set defaults in Settings. Reminders are local notifications, so they work without the app open and without internet.

How are free trials handled?

Switch on Free trial when you add a service, then enter the trial end date and the price after the trial. Trials appear at the top of Home with a countdown and reminders before they end.

Which currencies are supported?

Any currency with a three-letter code. If you use more than one, RenewRadar shows separate totals per currency instead of guessing exchange rates.

Can RenewRadar cancel subscriptions for me?

No. It reminds you in time, and you cancel with the service: in Google Play, your Apple account or on the service’s website.

Is there an iPhone version?

Not yet. RenewRadar is available for Android on Google Play.

What happens if I change phones?

Your list stays on the old phone, because nothing is synced to a server. Pro users can export a CSV copy. Pro itself is restored on a new phone with Restore purchase in Settings, using the same Google account.

My reminders arrive late. What can I do?

Some Android phones delay notifications to save battery. Set RenewRadar’s battery usage to unrestricted. Our guide to reliable reminders on Android has the steps.

How do I contact you?

Email renewradar@pixeldevcode.com. We read every message.

Where do I get it?

RenewRadar: Subscriptions on Google Play, by Pixel DevCode.
